**In brief**: OpenAI says a network apparently based in Iran used AI to write articles and posed as fake journalists to get them published on real news sites.

### Key points
- According to OpenAI, the network used AI to produce articles and submitted them to outside news outlets under fabricated journalist personas.
- The operation was traced to Iran. The initial report does not establish whether it had direct ties to the Iranian state.
- Details have not yet been made public, including how many outlets ran the pieces, what topics they covered, and how many readers they reached.
- The disclosure appears to follow OpenAI's regular reports on foreign influence operations that misuse its models.

### Why it matters
The case shows generative AI moving past social-media spam and into placing bylined content in actual news outlets under invented identities. Publishers that accept outside contributions will likely face more pressure to verify who their writers are, and AI companies will face higher expectations to detect this kind of misuse and disclose it.
